LanguageData.BF_UnknownTraitDesc: An unknown trait. It will reveal itself in time.
LanguageData.BF_TraitDiscoveredPack: {0} has revealed a hidden trait: {1}. It is now known on {2} of its packmates as well.
LanguageData.BF_MaterialTipDesc: Feels no pain, doesn't bleed or rot, and is immune to toxins. Butchering yields its material.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_LightsHint: Off: glowing creatures keep their look but light nothing up.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_LightFollowHint: How far a walking creature gets ahead of its light. Higher is cheaper with many glowing creatures; the light still recentres when it stops.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_EffectsHint: Embers, smoke and other effecters. Tints and glows always show.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_InheritHint: Multiplies each trait's own chance to pass to offspring.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_DiscoveryMessages: Message when a trait is discovered
LanguageData.BF_Settings_AbilityAI: Bastles use trait abilities on their own
LanguageData.BF_Settings_AbilityAIHint: Hostile, manhunting and tamed bastles cast their trait abilities in a fight, and wild ones when fighting back. Player colonists only cast when you order them to.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_UntrainedKnownAbilities: Untrained tamed bastles use known trait abilities
LanguageData.BF_Settings_UntrainedKnownAbilitiesHint: Tamed animals that haven't learned trait abilities still use the abilities of their known traits on their own. Turn this off to keep them from casting those until they are trained. Abilities from undiscovered traits are always used, since using them is how those traits are found.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_TrainedAbilitiesOnOwn: Trained bastles also use trait abilities on their own
LanguageData.BF_Settings_TrainedAbilitiesOnOwnHint: Tamed animals that have learned trait abilities keep casting them on their own as well as when you order them to. Turn this off to have them cast only on your order. With Ability AI, its autocast setting decides for the abilities it handles.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ArmorHint: Share of the stuff's armor value. Steel at this setting: +{0} sharp armor.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_DamageHint: How strongly the stuff's damage multipliers apply. 0%: every material hits like flesh.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_FireHint: How much flammability changes fire damage and ignition. At this setting: wood takes x{0} fire damage, stone x{1}.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ButcherHint: A steel bear (body size 2.15) gives about {0} steel.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_PreciousHint: Extra units for small-volume stuffs like gold and silver, as vanilla does.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_MarketValueHint: A tamed jade bear counts its jade toward colony wealth (and raid size).
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ValuePercent: Market value per trait point (% of creature's value)
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ValuePercentHint: Scales with the species: the same trait is worth far more on a thrumbo than on a rat. Drawbacks with negative points lower the value.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ValueFlatHint: Added on top of the percentage, so small bastles still count. Colony wealth, and so raid points, include every trait, known or not. Trade prices and the info card include only discovered traits.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_MaxNameTraitsHint: How many known traits can add a word to a bastle's name. The most notable traits are picked first, and at most one of them adds words after the creature's kind. The material always shows and is not counted.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_MysteryHint: Traders pay this much more (of the creature's normal value) for a creature with any undiscovered trait.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_PointTargetHint: Used when a mod rolls traits without its own target. Traits are rolled until their points reach the target; the last one may go over.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_StrictnessHint: How rarely a trait worth more than the points left still rolls. 0: the target is only a minimum. Higher keeps bastles close to their target.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_DrawbackHint: A bastle that rolls the chance can take drawbacks. Their negative points are paid back with more or better traits. The combat and utility rolls each make this check, and a utility drawback is only paid back with utility traits.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_UtilityHint: Utility traits (meaty, pack beast and the like) get their own roll after the others, in any trait slots left. Their points are this share of the bastle's target, at least one common trait's worth, and add no health.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_RarityShiftHint: Chance an inherited scaling trait is born one rarity higher or lower than its parent's (even odds either way).
LanguageData.BF_Settings_RarityWeightsHint: Relative weight of each rarity when a trait is rolled.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_RarityStrengthHint: How much stronger a scaling trait's effects are at each rarity.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_RarityPointsHint: What a trait is worth at each rarity: its cost when rolling, and its health and market value.
LanguageData.BF_DietCardNote: Changed by this creature's material and known bastle traits.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ScaledAttackCapHint: Attacks from traits such as Venomous hit as hard as the creature's own strongest attack. That base is capped at this, so a thrumbo's venom doesn't hit for its horn's 28. The trait's rarity multiplies the capped base, so a rarer trait always hits harder. 12 matches a cobra's bite.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_HealthPerPointHint: Each trait point makes every body part this much tougher. Utility trait points don't count. Traits can add more of their own.
LanguageData.BF_Card_TraitsIntro: Rare traits this creature was born with. Unknown traits reveal themselves in time, and offspring can inherit any of them.
LanguageData.BF_Card_Mystery: Traders pay {0} more for a creature with unknown traits.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_EatMaterial: Nutrition from eating own material (per unit)
LanguageData.BF_Settings_EatMaterialHint: A hungry material creature with no other food eats its own material: {0} units fill 1 nutrition. Tamed ones eat from your stockpiles unless the stack is forbidden; wild ones eat any they find.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_EatMaterialOffHint: Material creatures don't eat their material.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldEnabledHint: Turns every source on this tab on or off at once. Which sources are on is the default for a new game; a mod can switch them per colony when the game is created. The numbers here apply to every game.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldStrengthHint: Trait points a bastle gets from the threat points behind it. Straight lines between these, flat past either end.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WildStrengthHint: Share of the map's current raid points a wild bastle's traits are read from.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_ConvertedStrengthHint: Share of an animal event's or group's points read from the curve. Those bastles are extra danger: the event keeps its full size.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_OfferedStrengthHint: Share of the raid points where the animal is sold: the map a trader visits, or all your colonies together for settlements.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldHiddenHint: Their traits are hidden, except some of those a trader sells.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WildHint: On a new map and for every animal that wanders in later.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_AnimalEventsHint: Manhunter ambushes, herd migrations, thrumbo passes, farm animals wandering in, alphabeavers and frenzied animals. The whole group is one kind of bastle and shares what you learn about it. Manhunter packs are left to the bastle pack event below.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_GroupAnimalsHint: Pack animals and fighting animals in raids, caravans and settlement defences. They are added danger: the group keeps its size.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_TraderAnimalsHint: The trader knows some of each one's traits (none to all, at random).
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldOverridden: Set for this game by another mod. Change it there; this setting applies to new games.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldOverriddenBy: Set for this game. Change it in {0}; this setting applies to new games.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_WorldEventsHint: How often each happens against its base chance. 0 is never.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_SightingHint: One strong wild bastle passes through, to hunt or tame. It leaves if you let it be. Strength is the share of the map's raid points its traits are read from.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_PackHint: A manhunter pack of one bastle kind that shares what you learn about it. Points spent on traits leave the pack's size: it is that much smaller than a vanilla pack of the same threat, and every animal's traits are read from the event's full points.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_RampageHint: A single manhunting bastle wanders in, its traits all rare or better, with a pack's threat in its traits. Strength is the share of the event's points its traits are read from.
LanguageData.BF_Settings_HuntQuestHint: A faction asks you to kill a bastle and the manhunting pack it leads at a site nearby, for vanilla rewards. The bastle's traits are all rare or better, and the quest names one of them. Strength is the share of the site's threat points its traits are read from; the points spent on the bastle leave the pack's size.
LanguageData.BF_PackCalled: {PAWN_labelShort} called its pack. {1} came to fight.
LanguageData.BF_HydraSplit: {PAWN_labelShort} split as it died. {1} young ones sprang from its body.
